summary: mGBA scripting helper obscures gameplay after launcher start
symptom: The Scripting top-level window remains visible in front of gameplay after launch.

unexpected.predicted: A foreground launch exposes exactly one mGBA gameplay window before clients can pause the emulator.
unexpected.actual: mGBA --script unconditionally opens a Scripting top-level window and the prior close race did not reliably dismiss it.
diff: Expected one gameplay top-level window; observed gameplay plus Scripting.
Expected UI readiness before idle stop; the old helper raced RPC readiness and process suspension.

authority.oracle: macOS Accessibility window inventory for the exact clone PID must contain one AXStandardWindow whose title starts with mGBA, no title Scripting, followed by ps state containing T.
sources: System Events Accessibility API scoped by exact Unix PID
mGBA Qt source src/platform/qt/Window.cpp --script handling and ScriptingView.ui window title
SHA-256 checks of the disposable fixture and protected live checkpoint

steps: Launch mGBA with --script through the foreground launcher from a disposable savestate clone.
Wait for the Lua RPC bridge and inspect exact-PID top-level windows with Accessibility.
Confirm the original launcher path exposes the unconditional mGBA Scripting window and can be suspended before a focus-based close completes.
reproduction.observed: Before the fix, mGBA exposed a 480x348 gameplay window and an 843x665 Scripting window; source inspection proves --script opens ScriptingView unconditionally.

hypotheses.claim: The scriptingOpen configuration key suppresses the helper.
hypotheses.result: falsified: the --script Qt path calls scriptingOpen() unconditionally.

hypotheses.claim: A generic early Cmd-W reliably closes the helper.
hypotheses.result: falsified: it races window creation/focus and can be preempted by the client's SIGSTOP.

hypotheses.claim: Exact-PID Accessibility close after RPC readiness is deterministic.

root_cause.claim: mGBA's --script option unconditionally opens ScriptingView; the previous focus-based close raced Qt window creation and client idle suspension because RPC readiness did not imply UI cleanup readiness.
evidence: Qt source calls scriptingOpen(), openView(view), and script loading in the --script handler.
Accessibility observed both gameplay and Scripting windows on the affected live process.
Direct AXCloseButton activation for the exact Scripting title removed it without game input.
alternatives_falsified: focus-only Cmd-W is a sufficient launch synchronization boundary

solution.contract_change: Foreground launch now publishes MGBA_UI_READY_FILE only after exact-PID Accessibility closes every Scripting window, raises gameplay, and allows Qt destruction to complete; disposable clients wait for UI readiness before connecting and idle-stopping mGBA.

targeted_checks.name: two-launch exact-PID Accessibility UI replay
targeted_checks.evidence: Two clone launches each exposed exactly one mGBA AXStandardWindow, no Scripting window, and a T process state.

regression_checks.name: full Python suite
regression_checks.evidence: 105 tests passed; one opt-in macOS UI integration test skipped without its fixture environment variable.

replay.expected: One gameplay window, zero Scripting windows, and idle-stopped clone after observation.
replay.actual: Both runs reported one mGBA gameplay AXStandardWindow, zero Scripting windows, and process state T.

domain_knowledge: mGBA 0.11's Qt --script path opens ScriptingView regardless of scriptingOpen configuration.
tooling_contracts: MGBA_UI_READY_FILE, not RPC readiness, is the foreground launch boundary after which a client may suspend the emulator.
